title: Gen V Season 3 Story Details Officially Revealed After Cancellation & The Boys Series Finale
text:
The story could still happen elsewhere.
This article covers a developing story. Continue to check back with us as we will be adding more information as it becomes available. Warning: There are spoilers ahead for The Boys series finale.
Gen V season 3 is canceled, but Eric Kripke now reveals what the overarching story would have been. The news of the spinoff's cancellation came in the midst of The Boys season 5 releasing new episodes. Some of Gen V's characters do appear in the final of the franchise's main series, including Marie Moreau , Jordan Li , and Emma Meyer , but they ultimately play small roles and their stories remained unfinished.
In an interview with Variety after The Boys series finale, Kripke was asked if there were any story threads that would be explored in the franchise's future. The Boys creator and showrunner explained that Stan Edgar being reinstated as Vought CEO and having the corporation now reject supes would've been at the center of Gen V season 3, with the former Godolkin University students dealing with the fallout of these actions.
Check out Kripke's comments below: Had we done more Gen V, we were very clearly signaling in the finale that the torch was being passed from Annie to Marie for the good supe you’re following. I would love to find a way to continue that story. We’re in the very embryonic stage of seeing if there are any ideas that we’re really loving. It’s like all these loose nukes.
You have Stan Edgar basically disavowing relationships with superheroes, and so these people who have been coddled and protected this whole time are now suddenly out in the wild. Who tries to be Jessica Jones, and who tries to be a super villain? It leads to some really fascinating places that I would love to see, and the hope was we were going to put the Gen V kids in the middle of all that.
But hopefully we still will, and we can bring some of those characters into some of these stories that we’re talking about. Without giving the specifics away, yes, “Gen V” Season 3. The plot challenges they would have had to deal with were almost this metaphor of being a young adult, which is like you’re out in the world and there’s no infrastructure or jobs anymore.
How do you build a future for yourself, and how do you deal with certain superheroes who are just choosing to be villains? Gen V season 2 ended with the death of Thomas Godolkin , and now that Vought has disavowed supes, the college would not have continued.
Per Kripke's remarks, the spinoff would instead have explored Marie and her friends navigating the real world, which is no longer designed for them or for what they were learning at Godolkin. Instead, they would have been left to pick up the pieces of the mess that the Boys left behind after finally defeating Homelander .
This would have seen them helping supes who need guidance or are using their powers for good, while having to stop those who are using their new circumstances to become villains.
